terms.gloss: obscure, unclear, hard to make out
evidence: Hor. AP 25–26: brevis esse labōrō, obscūrus fīō
terms.comment: Literally “dark”: of words, writing and ideas, “indistinct, unintelligible” (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Brut. 152: ambigua prīmum vidēre, deinde distinguere
Cic. de Or. 2.110: sī est scrīptum aliquid ambiguē

phrases.english: I try to be brief, and I become obscure

phrases.latin: latentem explicāre dēfīniendō, obscūram explānāre interpretandō, ambigua prīmum vidēre, deinde distinguere
phrases.english: to bring out what is hidden by defining it, to make plain what is obscure by explaining it, first to see what is ambiguous and then to draw distinctions

sources: Lewis & Short: obscurus · Lewis & Short: ambiguus
